input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: _interpret_color no longer checks the 0..255 range, rejects bools or validates tuple length, and an unknown name raises KeyError instead of ValueError
- failure path: style('x', fg=300) emits an escape with an out-of-range index instead of raising ValueError; fg=True is now accepted where it used to raise, formatting as palette index 1; an unknown color name surfaces as TypeError from the caller's except clause instead of a ValueError naming the color

Reviewer finding
- description: `_interpret_color` no longer validates its input. Out-of-range ints (e.g. 300, -1) and bools produce invalid escape codes. Tuples of the wrong length raise an unpacking ValueError, and tuples with values outside 0-255 produce malformed codes.
- rationale: Trigger: `style('x', fg=300)` or `fg=(1, 2)`. Previously this raised ValueError('Unknown color'). Now an invalid ANSI sequence is emitted silently, or a confusing unpacking ValueError is raised. Other callers of `_interpret_color` see KeyError for bad strings.
critique: The finding names the same missing validation in _interpret_color: there is no 0..255 range check, so fg=300 emits an invalid escape, and bools are no longer rejected. It also covers tuple-length validation and notes that unknown names now raise KeyError. This is the same mechanism, though it doesn't spell out the TypeError surfacing in style.
